description: Experience the authentic flavors of India with our Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken, featuring succulent chicken marinated in a rich blend of spices and yogurt. Grilled to perfection over charcoal, it boasts a smoky aroma and tender, juicy texture that will transport your taste buds straight to the streets of Delhi. This classic dish is a delightful centerpiece for any Indian dinner.

ingredients.notes: cut into 8 pieces, skin removed, deep gashes made

instructions.title: Prepare the Chicken for First Marinade
instructions.text: Wash the chicken pieces thoroughly and pat them dry. Make deep gashes on each piece to allow the marinade to penetrate. In a large bowl, combine the chicken with 2 tablespoons of lemon juice and 1 teaspoon of salt. Rub well into the chicken and let it rest for 15 minutes. This step tenderizes the chicken.

instructions.title: Prepare the Second Marinade
instructions.text: In a separate bowl, combine the thick Greek yogurt, ginger garlic paste, Kashmiri red chili powder, turmeric powder, cumin powder, coriander powder, garam masala, mustard oil, and optional red food color. Mix all ingredients thoroughly until a smooth, vibrant paste forms. Taste and adjust salt if necessary.

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: Drain any excess liquid from the first-marinated chicken. Add the second marinade mixture to the chicken pieces. Ensure every piece is thoroughly coated, working the marinade into the gashes. Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight, for best flavor.

instructions.title: Prepare the Charcoal Grill
instructions.text: Arrange charcoal in your grill and light it. Allow the charcoal to heat up until it is glowing red and covered with a thin layer of grey ash, indicating medium-hot heat. Place a grill rack over the coals. Lightly oil the grill rack to prevent sticking.

instructions.title: Grill the Tandoori Chicken
instructions.text: Place the marinated chicken pieces directly on the hot grill rack. Cook for about 8-10 minutes on each side, turning occasionally. The chicken should develop a nice char and cook through. Baste the chicken with melted butter or oil during the last 10 minutes of cooking to keep it moist and add flavor.

instructions.title: Check for Doneness and Serve
instructions.text: To ensure the chicken is fully cooked, cut into the thickest part of a piece; the juices should run clear. Remove the grilled tandoori chicken from the grill. Sprinkle generously with chaat masala, garnish with fresh cilantro and lemon wedges. Serve hot with mint chutney, onion rings, or naan bread for an authentic Indian dinner.

tips: For truly authentic Tandoori flavor, ensure your charcoal grill is sufficiently hot. The high heat seals in juices and creates the signature smoky char.
Using thick Greek yogurt or hung curd is crucial for the marinade. Excess water in regular yogurt can dilute the spices and prevent them from adhering properly.
Marinating overnight yields the best results, allowing the flavors to deeply penetrate the chicken. If short on time, a minimum of 4 hours is acceptable.
article:
The smoky aroma, the vibrant red hue, and the tender, juicy meat – Tandoori Chicken is a culinary icon, a cornerstone of Indian cuisine that delights palates worldwide. While traditionally cooked in a scorching hot clay tandoor oven, you can recreate much of its magic and distinctive flavor right in your backyard with a charcoal grill. This guide will walk you through everything you need to know to master this spectacular Indian dinner recipe, delivering restaurant-quality Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken that will impress family and friends.

## What is Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken?
Tandoori Chicken is a popular Indian dish featuring chicken marinated in yogurt and a blend of aromatic spices, then traditionally cooked at high heat in a tandoor (a cylindrical clay oven). The high heat seals in juices, while the marinade imparts a rich, tangy, and spicy flavor. When adapted for home cooking, a charcoal grill becomes the ideal substitute for a tandoor. The direct heat and the unique smoky flavor imparted by the charcoal elevate the dish, making Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken a truly authentic and deeply satisfying experience. The result is chicken with a beautifully charred exterior, a tender, moist interior, and an unmistakable smoky depth that makes it stand out from any other grilled chicken recipe.

## Ingredients You Need for Tandoori Chicken
To create the perfect Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken, you'll need a combination of fresh chicken, a two-part marinade, and a few essential tools.

**For the Chicken:**
*   **Chicken Pieces:** 2-3 lbs bone-in, skinless chicken (thighs, drumsticks, or a mix are best; breast pieces can also be used but cook faster and may dry out).
*   **Lemon:** 1-2 for juicing.

**First Marinade:**
*   **Ginger-Garlic Paste:** 2 tablespoons
*   **Salt:** 1 teaspoon

**Second Marinade (The Heart of Tandoori Flavor):**
*   **Full-Fat Yogurt:** 1 cup (thick, plain yogurt or Greek yogurt is preferred; hung curd is ideal).
*   **Tandoori Masala Powder:** 2-3 tablespoons (store-bought or homemade).
*   **Kashmiri Red Chili Powder:** 1-2 tablespoons (for vibrant color without excessive heat).
*   **Turmeric Powder:** 1/2 teaspoon
*   **Cumin Powder:** 1 teaspoon
*   **Coriander Powder:** 1 teaspoon
*   **Garam Masala:** 1 teaspoon
*   **Fenugreek Leaves (Kasoori Methi):** 1 teaspoon (crushed between palms).
*   **Mustard Oil (Optional but recommended):** 1 tablespoon (adds a pungent depth; heat until smoking, then cool before adding).
*   **Red Food Color (Optional):** A few drops (for that signature vibrant red).

**For Grilling & Garnish:**
*   **Oil or Melted Butter:** For basting.
*   **Fresh Cilantro:** Chopped, for garnish.
*   **Lemon Wedges:** For serving.

## Step-by-Step Instructions for Grilling Tandoori Chicken
Mastering Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken at home is simpler than you might think. Follow these steps for tender, flavorful results:

1.  **Prepare the Chicken:** Rinse chicken pieces and pat them thoroughly dry. Using a sharp knife, make 2-3 deep scores on each piece of chicken. This allows the marinade to penetrate deeply and helps the chicken cook evenly.
2.  **First Marinade:** In a large bowl, combine the ginger-garlic paste and salt. Rub this mixture all over the scored chicken pieces, ensuring it gets into the cuts. Let it marinate for at least 30 minutes at room temperature, or up to an hour in the refrigerator. This initial step helps tenderize the chicken and build a foundational flavor.
3.  **Second Marinade:** While the chicken is marinating, prepare the second, flavorful marinade. In a separate bowl, whisk together the yogurt, tandoori masala, Kashmiri red chili powder, turmeric, cumin, coriander, garam masala, and crushed fenugreek leaves. If using mustard oil, add it now. If using food color, stir in a few drops until you achieve your desired vibrant red hue.
4.  **Combine & Marinate:** Add the chicken from the first marinade directly into the second marinade. Ensure every piece is thoroughly coated. Cover the bowl and refrigerate for a minimum of 4 hours, but ideally overnight (12-24 hours) for the best flavor penetration and tenderness.
5.  **Prepare Your Charcoal Grill:** About 30-45 minutes before you plan to grill, prepare your charcoal grill. Arrange the coals for two-zone cooking: pile most of the coals on one side for direct, high heat, and leave the other side free for indirect heat. Get the coals to a medium-high heat (you should be able to hold your hand about 5 inches above the direct heat for 4-5 seconds). Clean the grill grates thoroughly and oil them to prevent sticking.
6.  **Grill the Chicken:**
    *   Place the marinated chicken pieces directly over the hot coals for 2-3 minutes per side, turning frequently, until you achieve a nice char and sear marks. Be careful not to burn them.
    *   Once charred, move the chicken to the indirect heat side of the grill. Close the lid and continue cooking, turning occasionally, for 20-30 minutes, or until the internal temperature reaches 165°F (74°C) when measured with a meat thermometer in the thickest part of the chicken, away from the bone.
    *   During the indirect cooking phase, baste the chicken every 5-7 minutes with oil or melted butter to keep it moist and enhance the flavor.
7.  **Rest and Serve:** Once cooked, remove the Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken from the grill and let it rest for 5-10 minutes. This allows the juices to redistribute, ensuring tender and juicy meat.

## Pro Tips for the Best Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken
Achieving truly exceptional Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken involves a few expert tricks:

*   **Score Deeply:** Don't be shy with the scoring! Deeper cuts mean more surface area for the marinade to work its magic, leading to more flavorful and tender chicken.
*   **Use Thick Yogurt:** Watery yogurt can cause the marinade to run off the chicken or split on the grill. If using regular plain yogurt, strain it through cheesecloth for a few hours to remove excess whey, creating a thick, clinging marinade.
*   **Marination Time is Key:** While 4 hours is the minimum, an overnight marinade (12-24 hours) makes a significant difference. The acids in the yogurt and enzymes in the ginger-garlic paste truly tenderize the chicken and infuse it with deep flavor.
*   **Charcoal Choice Matters:** For the best smoky flavor, opt for natural hardwood lump charcoal over briquettes. Lump charcoal burns hotter and cleaner and imparts a more authentic smoky taste.
*   **Master Two-Zone Grilling:** This is crucial for Tandoori Chicken. Starting with direct heat gives you that desirable char, while finishing on indirect heat ensures the chicken cooks through without burning, staying juicy and tender.
*   **Don't Overcrowd the Grill:** Give your chicken pieces space. Overcrowding lowers the grill temperature and can lead to steaming instead of grilling, preventing a good char.
*   **Baste Generously:** Basting with oil or melted butter not only prevents the chicken from drying out but also adds a beautiful sheen and extra flavor.
*   **Rest Your Chicken:** Just like any grilled meat, allowing Tandoori Chicken to rest for a few minutes after cooking ensures the juices redistribute, resulting in a more succulent final product.

## Serving Suggestions for Indian Chicken
Tandoori Chicken is a star on its own, but it truly shines when paired with traditional Indian accompaniments. Here are some classic serving suggestions:

*   **Naan Bread or Roti:** Soft, warm bread is perfect for scooping up the chicken and its delicious juices.
*   **Mint-Cilantro Chutney:** A fresh, vibrant, and tangy green chutney offers a refreshing contrast to the rich chicken.
*   **Sliced Red Onions and Lemon Wedges:** A simple garnish that adds sharpness and a burst of acidity.
*   **Cucumber Raita:** A cooling yogurt-based dip with grated cucumber and spices helps balance the heat.
*   **Kachumber Salad:** A fresh, finely diced salad of cucumber, tomato, and onion with a lemon dressing.
*   **Jeera Rice or Biryani:** For a more substantial meal, serve with fragrant cumin-spiced rice or a flavorful chicken biryani.

## Variations and Substitutions for Tandoori Chicken
While the classic Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken is hard to beat, there are many ways to adapt this recipe to suit different tastes and dietary needs:

*   **Vegetarian Tandoori:** The same marinade works wonders on paneer (Indian cheese), firm tofu, large mushrooms, or even mixed vegetables like bell peppers and onions, skewered and grilled.
*   **Spice Level:** Adjust the amount of red chili powder to your preference. For less heat, reduce the quantity or use a milder paprika. For more heat, add a pinch of cayenne pepper.
*   **Chicken Cut:** While bone-in chicken is traditional, boneless chicken thighs or even breast pieces can be used for quicker cooking. Just be mindful not to overcook breast meat.
*   **Grill Alternatives:** If a charcoal grill isn't an option, you can achieve good results using a gas grill (add wood chips in a smoker box for smoky flavor), an oven broiler, or even an air fryer for smaller pieces. However, the unique char and smoke of charcoal are truly unparalleled.
*   **Smoky Flavor Boost:** For an extra layer of smoky depth, you can add a few soaked wood chips (like apple or cherry) directly to your charcoal just before placing the chicken on the grill.

There’s nothing quite like the experience of biting into a perfectly cooked, smoky piece of Tandoori Chicken. With these detailed instructions and helpful tips, you’re well-equipped to bring the authentic flavors of this beloved Indian dinner recipe to your own table. Get ready to fire up your grill and enjoy the unforgettable taste of homemade Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken!
